title: Predicting “priority” from “subject,body”
licence: Multilingual Customer Support Tickets. Licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (the creator’s current Hugging Face release). Commercial use: no. Non-commercial: experiments only. Don’t assume the current version permits training a model for a product that’s sold. The tickets are synthetic, and the versions share thousands of tickets, so never pool them.
setup: 20,000 texts, 3 labels, 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Character n-grams work across languages without a tokenizer.
decision: Best: words (tf-idf) + logistic regression, balanced accuracy 52% against 33% for always guessing the most common label. The data’s licence doesn’t allow commercial use, so no model is saved: this measures what’s possible, nothing more.
notes: 20,000 rows in the file; nothing removed; 20,000 measured.
By language (words (tf-idf) + logistic regression): de 47% of 8,077, en 56% of 11,923.
8,308 of these tickets (42%) also appear in aa_dataset-tickets-multi-lang-5-2-50-version.csv: the files are versions of one dataset, so each is measured on its own, never pooled.
